newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan disturbed by violent upsurge in S. Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Annan disturbed by violent upsurge in S. Lebanon.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan, disturbed at reports of renewed hostilities in southern Lebanon, urged both sides to take steps to prevent the situation from worsening, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.

"He is particularly concerned at the targeting of civilians, notably the killing of two youths by a roadside bomb in Kfar Houne and the subsequent shelling of the town of Sidon, with six reported killed and many more injured," U.N. spokesman Juan Carlos Brandt said in a statement.
Reports from the area said Sidon was shelled by a militia led by a pro-Israeli Lebanese commander, Antoine Lahd. There was no immediate word who planted the roadside bomb.

Brandt said the United Nations, which has a 4,475-member peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon, had been in touch with both sides and urged them to do their utmost to prevent a further deterioration of the situation and, in particular, to refrain from targeting civilians.

Pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas are battling to drive Israeli forces and their local militia allies from a 9-mile wide (15 kms) "security zone" set up to thwart attacks on northern Israel. The zone is the site of frequent clashes, roadside bombs and rocket attacks.
